Affect how the model picks the next word: coherence, variety, tendency to repeat.

At every step the model picks the next word from a list of candidates. These parameters control how widely it looks and how willing it is to take risks. If something breaks, the "Reset" button below restores the defaults.

Range: 0–2. Default 0.7.\nHow much risk the model takes when picking a word. Below 0.5 — answers are precise and predictable, but dry and repetitive; above 1.0 — livelier and more varied, but with a growing risk of nonsense and incoherence. 0 always picks the single most likely word.\nIf answers are boring and repetitive, raise it to 0.8–1.0. If the model "drifts" and rambles, lower it to 0.5–0.6.

Range: 0–1. Default 0.95.\nThe model only considers the most likely words whose combined probability doesn\'t exceed this value. 0.95 — drops the long "tail" of unlikely nonsense while keeping a wide choice. 0.5 — only the most obvious options.\nUsually doesn\'t need changing. If answers are still odd at a low temperature, try 0.9.

Range: 0–200. Default 40. 0 — disabled.\nA hard limit on how many top candidates are even considered. 40 means "pick from the 40 most likely words." Works alongside top-p — whichever constraint is stricter applies.\nLower (10–20) is stricter and more predictable, higher (80–100) is more varied.

Range: 1–2. Default 1.2. 1 — disabled.\nHow strongly the model avoids words it has already used recently. Without a penalty, small models like to loop and repeat the same phrase until the limit is hit.\nIf you see repetition or looping, raise it to 1.3–1.4. Too high (above 1.5) breaks normal speech: the model starts avoiding even necessary words like prepositions.

Typical values: 2048–8192. Default 4096. Local models only.\nHow much text the model keeps "in mind": chat history, file snippets, the system instruction. Roughly 1 token ≈ 3–4 characters of English text.\nHigher means the model remembers a longer conversation, but every model then uses noticeably more RAM, and on a phone that\'s a direct path to a crash. Only raise it if you have memory to spare, and lower it to 2048 if the app crashes on large models.

Range: 64–4096. Default 1024.\nThe ceiling on a single answer\'s length — the model stops here, or earlier if it decides the answer is complete on its own. Doesn\'t affect how much the model remembers, only how much it can say at once.\nLower it if answers are too long or generation feels noticeably slow. Raise it for tasks that need a long, coherent piece of text — but the higher the limit, the more likely a small model drifts or loops by the end.

Several keys for one provider form a pool. The app always uses the first key that isn\'t currently paused. If a provider replies "daily quota exceeded," that key is automatically paused for 24 hours and the app moves on to the next key in the list instead of just showing an error.
